core_obligations: Split X into disjoint open pieces with constant coefficient (proof lines 4360-4375): choose a pro-etale covering trivializing F, say F restricted to U_i is the constant sheaf on M_i; then U_i x_X U_j is empty whenever M_i and M_j are not isomorphic, so for each module M the union U_M of the images of the U_i with M_i isomorphic to M is open by the openness of images of fpqc coverings, and X is the disjoint union of the U_M; replacing X by U_M one may assume all M_i equal to a single M.

Form the torsor of isomorphisms (proof lines 4377-4383): the sheaf of isomorphisms from the constant sheaf on M to F is a torsor for the sheaf of automorphisms of the constant sheaf on M, which is the constant sheaf on the group of Lambda-module automorphisms of M.

Conclude (proof lines 4383-4387): since torsors for the etale and pro-etale topologies agree, the sheaf of isomorphisms has sections etale locally on X, so F is etale locally constant, which is the assertion that the pullback is essentially surjective on the category of locally constant sheaves of finite presentation; the other direction and faithfulness are immediate.
proof_roadmap: Trivialize the sheaf on a pro-etale covering and split the base into disjoint open pieces on which the trivializing module is constant.
Replace the sheaf by a torsor of isomorphisms under the automorphism sheaf of a constant sheaf.
Use the agreement of torsors between the two topologies to conclude that the sheaf is etale locally constant.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a scheme X and a ring Lambda the pullback along the comparison morphism defines an equivalence between the locally constant sheaves of Lambda-modules of finite presentation on the etale site and on the pro-etale site (statement lines 4337-4358). The proof (proof lines 4360-4388) trivializes the sheaf on a pro-etale covering, splits the base into disjoint open pieces by the openness of images of fpqc coverings, forms the torsor of isomorphisms with a constant sheaf, and concludes by the agreement of torsors for the two topologies.
